fine_trace.code: md_is_link_title(MD_CTX* ctx, const MD_LINE* lines, MD_SIZE n_lines, OFF beg, OFF* p_end, MD_SIZE* p_beg_line_index, MD_SIZE* p_end_line_index, OFF* p_contents_beg, OFF* p_contents_end)
fine_trace.note: Input-controlled offset `beg` from the caller enters the title parser; it points into the text buffer after a '[' opener and '(' in an inline link spec.
Whitespace skip advances `off`; if it reaches the line end, line_index is incremented and off is set to the next line's beg.

fine_trace.code: switch(CH(off)) { case _T('"'): closer_char = _T('"'); break; case _T('\''): closer_char = _T('\''); break; case _T('('): closer_char = _T(')'); break; default: return FALSE; }
fine_trace.note: The first non-whitespace character determines the closing delimiter; off is then incremented past the opening quote/paren.

The loop bound `line_end` is taken from the MD_LINE array without verifying that `lines[line_index].end` is within `ctx->size`. When the caller passes a `lines` array whose last line's `end` field exceeds the actual text buffer length, the inner loop reads past the heap buffer.

fine_trace.code: while(off < line_end) { if(CH(off) == _T('\\') && off+1 < ctx->size && (ISPUNCT(off+1) || ISNEWLINE(off+1))) { off++; } else if(CH(off) == closer_char) { ... } else if(closer_char == _T(')') && CH(off) == _T('(')) { return FALSE; } off++; }
fine_trace.note: `CH(off)` expands to `ctx->text[off]`; when `off` reaches `line_end` which is beyond `ctx->size`, this reads out of bounds, causing the heap-buffer-overflow READ 1.
